## Fatal findings

1. [`thm-local-ring-unit-characterisations`](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-local-ring-unit-characterisations.md:4) — title.

   The title asserts the three-way characterization unconditionally, but the Statement begins, “Assume the Axiom of Choice,” and proof step 1.1 invokes the maximal-ideal existence theorem, whose on-disk Statement also explicitly assumes Choice. The title therefore asserts more than the proved theorem.

   Severity: **fatal** — title overclaim/missing choice hypothesis.

2. [`cor-every-local-ring-is-its-localisation-at-its-maximal-ideal`](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/cor-every-local-ring-is-its-localisation-at-its-maximal-ideal.md:25) — Statement, `[F1]`, and proof step 1.1.

   The Statement has no choice hypothesis. `[F1]` says that in a local ring the maximal ideal is exactly the set of nonunits, but its cited dependency states:

   > “Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a nonzero commutative ring \(R\), the following are equivalent…”

   Step 1.1 uses this omitted hypothesis to conclude every denominator outside \(\mathfrak m\) is already a unit. Thus the cited result’s hypothesis has been dropped.

   Severity: **fatal** — missing choice hypothesis and inaccurate dependency restatement.

3. [`cor-local-rings-have-only-trivial-idempotents`](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/cor-local-rings-have-only-trivial-idempotents.md:25) — Statement, `[F1]`, and proof steps 1.1–2.1.

   The unconditional Statement relies entirely on `[F1]`, the assertion that one of \(x\) and \(1-x\) is a unit in every local ring. The cited `thm-local-ring-unit-characterisations` proves that assertion only under the Axiom of Choice. Neither this item’s Statement nor Given carries that hypothesis.

   Severity: **fatal** — missing choice hypothesis and inaccurate dependency restatement.

No other defect meeting the brief’s reporting threshold was found.

The load-bearing checks otherwise passed: the localisation relation uses the necessary auxiliary multiplier in transitivity; both fraction operations are proved representative-independent; \(0\in S\) is handled consistently; both universal properties prove uniqueness; the fraction-field interface supplies the construction, embedding, and rational-function specialization; and the prime-ideal clause is locally proved. Its external attribution is also correctly divided: [Stacks Lemma 10.9.16](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CM) supplies only the ideal statement, while [Stacks Lemma 10.17.5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00E3) supplies the prime correspondence.

The splitting-field existence and isomorphism inductions decrease degree correctly. The factorial result uses explicit power coordinates and spanning only, not extension dimension. The normality descent, nonempty-intersection, algebraic-splitting, and finite-support generation arguments close as stated.

Coverage: I read all 56 assigned items and all four page files fully. I opened the exact relevant Definition/Statement sections of all 53 external dependency targets, inspected the batch notes and the load-bearing proof-contract entries, verified the batch contracts match the merged contracts, and ran the strict contract check successfully over 49/49 proof-bearing items. No assigned item was merely sampled, no dependency target was `ai-generated`, and nothing was unavailable.
